findings.failing_input: TikTok FX succeeds (ttSpendCad !== null) but the daily run's return value path (line 1121-1126) computes `roas = revenueCad / merged.totalSpendCad` using merged.totalSpendCad — which EXCLUDES TikTok. The persisted data_daily row at line 437-439 correctly uses `totalSpendCadAll = merged.totalSpendCad + ttSpendCad`. So the DB row and the return value disagree for TikTok-enabled stores.
findings.expected: Both the persisted data_daily.roas/grossProfit/netProfit AND the returned RunDailyResult.roas/grossProfit/netProfit should use the SAME total-spend basis (i.e. include TikTok when ttSpendCad is non-null).
findings.actual: Lines 1121-1126 build the return value from `merged.totalSpendCad` (no TikTok), but lines 437-449 write to disk a row that DOES include TikTok in roas/gross_profit/net_profit. For uzoshop (the only TikTok store) the returned roas underreports total spend in the denominator, so the returned roas > the dashboard roas.
findings.fix_sketch: After persist-batch completes, compute the return value using the same `totalSpendCadAll` logic (handling the FX-failed null branch). E.g. read the per-store fxCache + ttSpendCad from a top-level let, or recompute consistently. Simplest fix: hoist `ttSpendCad`/`totalSpendCadAll`/`roas`/`grossProfitCad`/`netProfitCad` out of the persist-batch closure into outer variables, and use them in the return.
findings.regression_test_idea: Pin: with tiktokSpend.spend=40 USD + fxRate=1.35 + merged.totalSpendCad=86 CAD + revenueCad=1234 CAD: `result.roas` should equal `1234 / (86 + 40*1.35) = 8.79`, NOT `1234 / 86 = 14.35`. Pre-fix the test asserting `result.roas === 1234/86` would pass; post-fix it should be 1234/(86+54) ≈ 8.79.

findings.failing_input: Supabase `.upsert(...)` resolves with `{ error: PostgrestError | null }` — it does NOT reject on RLS/schema errors. The mock in cronDaily.test.ts:438-441 sets `throwIn === 'upsert' → return Promise.resolve({ error: { message: 'upsert-failed' } })` and the writer DOES check `if (error) throw`. Good. BUT: many of the persist-batch sub-upserts (orders_attribution, product_catalog, etc.) also check `error`. Looks consistent across all the explicit calls — VERIFIED. NOT a bug. Withdrawn.

cadFor's fxCache is keyed only by currency code (`cur`). Within a single persist-batch step.run, multiple FX retries against the SAME currency that all transiently failed would all be cached as `null` after the first failure. If the FIRST cadFor call for ILS happens to hit a transient Frankfurter 5xx, every subsequent ILS row in the SAME step skips its CAD update — even if a retry 200ms later would have succeeded. The cache turns one transient blip into a full per-platform persist skip for that tick.
findings.expected: Either (a) don't cache `null` (re-attempt per row), or (b) cache with a short expiry, or (c) accept the trade-off but document it.
findings.actual: Cache caches `null` for the lifetime of the persist-batch step. The Inline comment at 482-483 explicitly documents this as intentional ('Cache failures too (null sentinel) so we don't hammer Frankfurter with retries inside the same persist-batch'). So it's a deliberate trade-off — but at the operator scale (3 stores × 1 daily run + a few sync-now clicks/month) the 'don't hammer' concern is essentially zero, and the cost is potentially losing a full day of FX-denominated columns to one transient blip.
findings.fix_sketch: Either retry once on null, or remove the null caching: `if (rate === null) { fxCache.delete(cur); }` — next row's cadFor call would re-attempt the rate fetch. At the daily cadence (one persist-batch per cron-daily run per store) the Frankfurter hammer-fear is unfounded.
findings.regression_test_idea: Mock getFxRate to fail on the first call and succeed on the second. Pin: in a single persist-batch, expect the second ILS row to land with `spend_cad` populated (rate retried), not omitted (rate=null still cached).

findings.failing_input: Shopify product row with fractional units (e.g. a partial refund of 0.5 units after gift-card payment dust). `units: Math.round(p.units)` and `orders: Math.round(p.orders)` will round 0.5 → 0 (banker's rounding) or 1 (half-away-from-zero) depending on JS engine. Lost precision for the dashboard's per-product unit count.
findings.expected: Document the rounding rationale OR migrate the BIGINT columns to NUMERIC. The same TODO already exists for the BIGINT campaigns_daily columns at lines 622-631.
findings.actual: Silent loss of <1 unit precision per row. At operator scale (~50 products/day) this is negligible — but the rounding could legitimately flip a 0.6 unit refund display to 1 (overstating refund count) or 0 (understating).
findings.fix_sketch: Same as the BIGINT comment at 622-631 — long-term fix is a NUMERIC schema migration. Short-term: document the loss in the inline comment so future devs know not to expect sub-unit fidelity.

uncertainty_notes: Finding INN-01 is the highest-confidence concern: the return-value vs persisted-row mismatch is concrete and reproducible. INN-03 is a deliberate trade-off per the inline comment but the operator's actual usage pattern makes the trade-off lopsided. INN-02 was investigated and withdrawn — every Supabase call in persist-batch explicitly destructures `{ error }` and throws on truthy error.
